title: Line-middle graph inequality conjecture for outer-connected domination
source: Farshad Kazemnejad, Behnaz Pahlavsay, Elisa Palezzato and Michele Torielli, “Connected and outer-connected domination number of middle graphs”, arXiv:2206.15439 (2022). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.15439)

lanes.final_paper_and_definition_check: final-paper-check-358270-355218-opus-20261118-r1/CHECK-355218.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; definitions literal; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: Conjecture 7.6 of the source (the outer-connected domination number of the line graph is at most that of the middle graph) is false: for every h >= 2 the graph formed by two copies of K_{2h} joined by a three-edge path has outer-connected domination number 2h+2 for its middle graph and C(2h,2)+h+1 for its line graph (6 against 9 at h = 2), under both conventions for an empty complement. Lean proves explicit bounds giving the strict inequality for every h and infinitely many counterexample orders; the exact values are proved in the paper. Significance is low; this is a second result from section 7 of the same source as accepted 355217.
significance.caveat: Low significance, and a second credit from the same source section as 355217 (user may overrule). Lean proves bounds sufficient for the refutation; exact values are in the written proof only.

root_basis: Root extracted the modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, object hashes identical to the author build, axioms exactly the allowed three), and screened the omega registry. An independent Opus referee read the paper line by line, confirmed the Lean definitions are literal renderings of the source definitions, and recomputed small cases; its editorially revised copy is the accepted paper.
